messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-INC-4321 for service=redwood-api-hosted. Summary=5xx spike on /v1/generate. Priority=P1. Page sent to primary oncall Amanda (oncall). Link: https://pd/redwood/PD-INC-4321 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Escalation policy 'prod-oncall' configured: primary=Amanda (oncall) -> secondary=Tarun -> manager=DevOps Manager. If no ack in 6m escalate to secondary, 12m escalate to manager.

Amanda (oncall): Acking now, saw a few alerts pop. I'm in a meeting for next 10m but will try to pull logs quickly. Assigning to @Tarun if I can't keep eyes.

(pagerduty-bot automated note at +6m): Escalation: alert PD-INC-4321 auto-escalated to secondary Tarun due to missed ack window from Amanda.

Tarun: Acknowledged. Taking point. Adding myself to PD incident PD-INC-4321. First steps: collecting recent runtime logs and tailing inference pods.

Tarun: Quick snapshot: /v1/generate 5xx rate jumped ~18% starting 00:11:03 UTC, p50 latency up from 120ms -> 450ms. Error traces show repeated backend connection errors to runtime-worker-3 and OOM-ish logs.

Li Wei: Are dedicated customers affected or just hosted?

Tarun: Looks isolated to hosted API pool in us-west-2. Dedicated pools unaffected. CS looped in. Notifying customer success now.

Maria: We rolled a small runtime change ~00:08 that touched batch-scheduler. I can revert if you want. Suggested rollback command: ```kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-runtime -n inference --to-revision=20260314-3b2f```

Tarun: Please hold on rollback until I try to trigger model-fallback. If rollback doesn't reduce 5xx quickly we'll revert. Starting fallback to model-variant `gptx-base-quant` for hosted route to reduce mem pressure. Command: `redwoodctl route set-fallback --route /v1/generate --variant gptx-base-quant`

DevOps Manager: I've been auto-escalated as manager (missed ack). Keeping an eye. Please add customer impact and ETA. I'll coordinate with CS for any external comms.

Tarun: Fallback applied at +12m. Immediate improvement: 5xx dropped to 2% within ~90s, p50 latency back to ~160ms. Continuing to monitor for regressions.

Amanda (oncall): Back from meeting. Sorry for the gap — I wasn't able to ack in the window. Handing off to Tarun fully, happy to assist with postmortem.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-4321 acknowledged by Tarun, status=acknowledged. Notes updated.

Tarun: Rolling back the runtime change now as a precaution (per Maria). Executing: ```kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-runtime -n inference --to-revision=20260314-3b2f``` Monitor will take ~2m.

Tarun: Rollback completed at +22m. No further 5xx spike. Will keep the fallback variant active for 15m then gradually restore routing once full confidence.

Li Wei: Thanks. Any customer-facing impact? CS: estimate how many customers saw errors and what's the communication plan?

DevOps Manager: CS reports approx 12 customers had intermittent 5xx errors, highest impacted were trial accounts and a small ecommerce customer (now recovered). No SLA breach for dedicated customers. Preparing a short incident notification to affected customers.

Tarun: Mitigated. Closing PD incident now. Root cause likely a bad scheduler change that increased memory churn on hosted runtime leading to transient worker failures; rollback + model-fallback fixed.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-4321 resolved by Tarun. Duration ~25 minutes.

Amanda (oncall): Thanks everyone for the quick follow-through. I'll own the postmortem and include timeline, missed-ack escalation notes, and follow-up: improve ack handover doc + adjust PD window to 4m primary -> 6m secondary to reduce manager escalations. :thumbsup:

DevOps Manager: Good call on the handover doc. We'll review escalation timings and oncall staffing. Adding action: update runbook to explicitly call out model-fallback first step.

Maria: I'll open the revert PR audit and run additional load tests on the scheduler change.

Tarun: Closing thread in Slack, will publish incident summary in #postmortems and link to PD-INC-4321. Good work team. :white_check_mark:
